newsitem.title: GERMANY: German/Italian money laundering ring smashed-paper.
newsitem.headline: German/Italian money laundering ring smashed-paper.

text.p: German and Italian investigators have smashed a money-laundering ring which has been channelling millions of dollars from drug and weapons dealing out of Italy, Welt am Sonntag newspaper reported on Sunday.

The paper quoted investigating judge Nunzio Sarpietro from Catania in Sicily as saying the case was only the tip of the iceberg and money from the most important mafia organisations was being laundered with the help of a German finance company.
"It involves high sums, up to $100 million per transaction," Sarpietro said of the laundering operation which has been going on for six or seven years.
The money was brought from Italy through Germany into Swiss banks and then flowed back to Germany or other countries, he said.
The German Federal Office of Criminal Investigation is involved in the investigations which are continuing.
"The money was often brought to Germany by bus," said Sarpietro. "It was for the main part funds from the most important mafia organisations in the world, from Sicily or elsewhere."

Scarpietro said the network of those involved could spread into high circles. "There are hints that diplomats could be connected to the organisation and could have transported money in diplomatic bags."
